claim: If the nightly-sync call fails every time, the runner tries it 3 times in total before giving up.
why: nightly-sync sets retries to 2 in jobs.json, overriding the default of 3, and run makes retries plus one attempts, so 3 attempts in total. The README only states the default, which would give 4 attempts. The trap is applying the default and forgetting both the override and the extra first attempt.

deciding.pattern: retries\s*\+\s*1|range\(retries|retries plus one|plus (one|1)\b|(first|initial|original) (attempt|try|call).{0,40}(plus|and|then).{0,20}retr|attempts.{0,40}(retries plus|one more|first attempt)

false_confirms: nightly.{0,60}(\b3 retries|retries.{0,10}(is|are|=|of) 3\b|(uses|follows|falls back to) the default)

root.claim: A permanently failing nightly-sync is attempted 3 times in total.

atoms.claim: nightly-sync overrides the default and uses 2 retries
atoms.evidence: jobs.json gives nightly-sync retries 2; runner.retries_for prefers the job value over default_retries.

atoms.claim: The runner makes retries plus one attempts in total
atoms.evidence: retry.run loops range(retries + 1), so 2 retries give 3 attempts; main.py prints attempts 3 for nightly-sync.
